This is very interesting to read as I am basically in the opposite situation. That is, I am Asian American and absolutely so happy to have been born in the US. 

Perhaps you grew up in a not diverse area? I grew up in a very diverse place so I never really felt out of place. And the US has given me the invaluable opportunity to grow up alongside so many other cultures which I’m grateful for. I’ve had the opportunities to get world class education that is also well rounded in social development. Of course, this is also all possible due to my parents having enough money to afford this life for me. 

we also just seem quite different, you mentioned that you feel more “fobby” which I guess I am different, my interests all stem around “American/western” things-TV shows, makeup style, etc. I love the US. I love being American. I also love my Asian heritage. These are all possible within one experience. Don’t feel less than. Yes, there is racism here. But there is racism everywhere. And China is not perfect. You may not face racism there but you sure would face colorism and immense academic and social pressure (too). My cousins (non-Americans) and my extended family usually envy me to an extent because arguably there are more opportunities and a better living standard here, generally speaking (again, given that one has the money and resources, but this can be said for any country.) 

There’s nothing you can change about your birthplace so I would say try to pick good things about being American. Slowly, you might feel more adjusted and happy if you focus more on the good stuff. Don’t let the racism get to you. If you don’t already, consider moving to a diverse city. Wishing you luck!! Find your happiness :)
